title: Theo and the Garden
premise: Freya Sandoval, a mercenary sworn to a god that fell silent fifteen years ago, has survived in the city of Vharen by selling harmless charms in a realm that outlawed magic. When her new lover, a quiet gardener named Theo, turns out to be the figure named in a century-old book of prophecies, he is seized by the city's witch-hunters and marked for execution as the prophesied 'Bridge.' Freya must choose between her oath of neutrality and the man she loves, uncovering that her silent god was imprisoned by the very covenant Theo is destined to reforge. Together they break into the god-prison beneath the city's garden, where Theo must sacrifice his ordinary identity to become the living bridge between realms — and Freya, breaking her oath, becomes the first priestess of a new covenant. The book ends with magic legal, the god reborn through Theo's transformed self, and Freya choosing love not instead of duty but as the shape duty finally takes.
about_author: Gideon Kavanagh is the pen name of a former botanical archivist who spent a decade cataloguing rare manuscripts in monastery libraries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about quiet people caught in enormous machinery, and tend an actual garden that they insist is unremarkable.

chapters.title: The Charmseller's Stall
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She sells a luck-charm to a nervous clerk, hiding the dead weight of her broken oath beneath market-day banter. Introduce Vharen's magic ban and the witch-hunters' patrols. Emotional beat: weary competence masking grief for her silent god.

chapters.title: The Man Who Grew Things
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She meets Theo, a gardener restoring the abandoned municipal garden, when she buys cut flowers she doesn't need. Their flirtation is awkward and real. Emotional beat: first warmth in fifteen years, and guilt about enjoying it.

chapters.title: Third Date, Old Book
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In Freya's apartment he finds her copy of the Vharen Codex, a century-old prophecy text, and idly reads a passage aloud — describing himself, tonight's date, word for word. Emotional beat: uncanny dread turning a cozy evening cold.

chapters.title: What the Codex Says
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They decode the prophecy together: a 'Bridge' will reforge the broken covenant between realms, and the god beneath the garden will wake. Theo laughs it off; Freya cannot. Emotional beat: intimacy strained by a truth one of them already believes.

chapters.title: The Knock at the Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Witch-hunters arrive with the Codex's page memorized. Theo is taken for questioning as a prophesied subversive; Freya hides, sworn to neutrality, hating herself for it. Emotional beat: cowardice as a conscious, agonizing choice.

chapters.title: The Oath That Went Quiet
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, flashback-heavy. Fifteen years ago her god answered her final prayer with silence, and the covenant collapsed, making all magic illegal. She recalls the day the sky over Vharen went gray. Emotional beat: understanding that her silence and her god's may share a cause.

chapters.title: Cells Beneath the Hall
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In custody he meets other 'prophetic matches' — frauds and fanatics — and a dying old woman who recognizes his birthmark and calls him 'root-stock.' Emotional beat: terror hardening into a strange sense of belonging.

chapters.title: A Bribe of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She trades her last true charms to a corrupt hunter for access to the cells. First use of real magic in years, and it works — because Theo is near. Emotional beat: hope arriving through an act of betrayal against her own rules.

chapters.title: The Garden at Midnight
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Freya breaks Theo out; they flee through the overgrown garden, where plants turn toward him as he passes. The old woman's words begin making sense. Emotional beat: fugitive intimacy, love accelerating under pressure.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Hedgerows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A chase through the garden's maze; Freya fights for the first time as an outlaw, not a neutral. She kills a hunter and cannot unsee it. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Ash
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They seek a defrocked priestess, Maren, who keeps the Codex's suppressed final chapter: the covenant was not broken by the god — it was broken by the city, which imprisoned the god to monopolize its power. Emotional beat: righteous fury reframing fifteen years of grief.

chapters.title: Root and Stock
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Maren reveals Theo's lineage: descendants of the god's first gardeners, bred to be the Bridge. Theo rages at having been made a vessel without consent. Emotional beat: identity crisis — is he a man or an instrument?

chapters.title: The City Closes Its Fist
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Vharen locks down; the High Hunter declares Theo a demon and the garden will be burned at dawn. Ordinary citizens Freya has charmed for years begin sheltering the fugitives. Emotional beat: quiet solidarity of the small people.

chapters.title: What Freya Swore
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers Freya's old oath-token and learns her god's silence coincides with the city's imprisonment — her patron is the prisoner. Her neutrality was never cowardice; it was mourning. Emotional beat: forgiveness and deeper love.

chapters.title: The Door Under the Roses
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Following Maren's map, they find the god-prison beneath the garden's oldest rose tree: a door that answers to Freya's oath-token and Theo's blood together. Emotional beat: awe, and the realization the prophecy needs both of them, not one.

chapters.title: The God in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They descend and find the god — small, withered, a seed of light kept starving for a century. It recognizes Freya and cannot speak, only grieve. Emotional beat: heartbreak; divinity rendered helpless and human-scaled.

chapters.title: The High Hunter's Sermon
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Above, the city prepares the garden's burning as public spectacle. The High Hunter, revealed to be a former oath-sworn mercenary who chose power over faith, offers Freya Theo's life for her silence renewed. Emotional beat: temptation as a mirror of her past self.

chapters.title: Reforging
chapters.summary: Both POVs, climax begins. As the garden burns above, Theo and Freya attempt the covenant: Freya must surrender her oath entirely, and Theo must let the god root in him — dissolving his ordinary self. The god hesitates, refusing to consume him. Emotional beat: sacrifice met with mercy.

chapters.title: The Bridge Stands
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, climax. Theo chooses it freely — the one thing the prophecy never required. He becomes the Bridge: still himself, but rooted in both realms. The god blooms through him, the fire dies mid-roar, and every outlawed charm in Vharen lights at once. Emotional beat: transcendence earned by consent.

chapters.title: Ash and Testimony
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The High Hunter falls, undone by the crowd of citizens who witnessed the miracle. Freya testifies before the council — not as a mercenary but as the first priestess of the restored covenant. Emotional beat: justice achieved outside and then inside the law.

chapters.title: The New Gardener
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Magic is legalized; Theo tends the garden, now half in this world and half in the god's, teaching others the old growing-arts. He is changed but not lost. Emotional beat: gentle wonder, identity integrated rather than erased.

chapters.title: Theo and the Garden
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. A year on, Freya and Theo marry in the garden at dusk. Her god speaks her name for the first time in sixteen years — through the roses, through him. Emotional beat: love and duty reconciled as one covenant, quietly kept.
